scope.description: One-row deepening tranche for Steelix, the Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 5 insert released March 1, 2000, emphasizing Trainer Magazine distribution, Benimaru Itoh art, Metal-type Johto weight, Gold/Silver symbol, bonus-card border text, and traps against Neo/Gold-Silver Steelix, English Neo Genesis, Jasmine's Steelix, Shining Steelix, and generic Steelix listings.

chase_cards.name: Steelix
chase_cards.why: This is a chase because it is a magazine-borne Johto heavyweight: Steelix gets a dedicated Trainer Magazine promo with Benimaru Itoh's harder-edged art and the new Metal identity made physical.

key_artists.name: Benimaru Itoh
key_artists.why: Itoh matters here because Steelix is a creature of weight, texture, and mechanical force. His Pokemon background also crosses into 3D modeling and Creatures-era production, which makes this card feel close to the machinery of Pokemon, not only the card frame.

claims.text: The local catalog models the Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 5 insert as a one-row unnumbered promotional source group containing Steelix at source index 158.
Bulbapedia says this Steelix was available as an Unnumbered Promotional card included in Volume 5 of Pokemon Card Trainers magazine, released on March 1, 2000.
PokeBoon also describes the Steelix promo as Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 5 with distribution date March 1, 2000, and tags the source as Book / Unopened.
A collector-maintained Trainer Magazine promo list records the early insert sequence as Vol. 1 Snap Pikachu, Vol. 3 Bilingual Exeggutor, Vol. 4 Murkrow & Darkness Energy, and Vol. 5 Steelix.
The official Pokemon site lists Pokemon Gold and Silver as released in Japan on November 21, 1999, placing this March 2000 Steelix magazine promo in the early Johto period.
Bulbapedia credits the Steelix illustration to Benimaru Itoh.
PokeBoon also credits this Steelix promo to Benimaru Itoh.

Bulbapedia's Benimaru Itoh page says he is a manga artist, designer, and musician; at Creatures, Inc. he worked as 3D modeling director for the Pokemon Stadium series and illustrated Pokemon Newspaper Strip comics and several Pokemon TCG card artworks.
Bulbapedia identifies the card as Steelix LV.57, Japanese name ハガネール Haganeil, Metal-type Stage 1 evolving from Onix, HP 100, and National Pokédex number 208.
Bulbapedia says the card features the Gold, Silver, to a New World... symbol and that the bottom card border reads Pokemon Card Official Magazine 'Trainers Vol. 5' bonus card.

The card matters because it makes early Johto's Metal identity feel tactile: Steelix is not only a species label, but a magazine-distributed object where Onix becomes industrial, heavy, and newly typed.

special_identification_instructions.trigger: A listing, want, scan, seller story, or agent memory says Steelix, Haganeil, ハガネール, No.208, Trainers Vol. 5, Pokemon Card Trainers, March 1 2000, Benimaru Itoh, Metal Crash, Rumble, Neo Genesis, Gold/Silver Steelix, Jasmine's Steelix, Shining Steelix, or magazine promo.
special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify Trainers Vol. 5 Steelix by magazine-insert route, Benimaru Itoh credit, Metal-type Stage 1 text, Gold/Silver symbol, and Trainers Vol. 5 bonus-card border text before trusting species-only Steelix memory.
steps: Confirm the release route is Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 5 insert, released March 1, 2000.
Confirm the card is Steelix / ハガネール Haganeil, National Pokédex No. 208, as an unnumbered Japanese promotional card.
Preserve Benimaru Itoh as illustrator and do not silently replace the credit with Ken Sugimori from the Neo/Gold-Silver expansion Steelix.
Check for Metal-type Stage 1 frame, HP 100, evolution from Onix, and attacks Metal Crash / メタルクラッシュ and Rumble / じひびき where image quality allows.
Check for the Gold, Silver, to a New World... symbol and bottom-border text reading Pokemon Card Official Magazine 'Trainers Vol. 5' bonus card.

Separate Japanese Gold/Silver to a New World Steelix, English Neo Genesis Steelix, Jasmine's Steelix, Shining Steelix, Mysterious Mountains Steelix, Wind from the Sea Steelix, and modern Steelix cards unless source evidence proves this exact row.
Request front/back seller photos, holo/surface evidence, and magazine provenance separately from catalog identity.

narrative.human_title: Steelix: metal enters through the magazine spine
narrative.why_it_matters: This Steelix has the right kind of weight. It is not just Onix evolved; it is Johto's new Metal grammar arriving as a Trainer Magazine object, with Benimaru Itoh giving the serpent a harder, stranger body than the neat Sugimori expansion card. That matters for collectors because the assembly is visible: magazine route, bonus-card border text, Gold/Silver symbol, and a creature whose whole identity is pressure made solid. The card feels like early-2000 Pokemon learning to be industrial.

claims.text: The local catalog identifies row 158 as Steelix, a Metal Pokemon row in the Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 5 insert source group.
Bulbapedia lists the card as Steelix LV.57, Japanese name ハガネール Haganeil, Metal-type Stage 1 evolving from Onix, HP 100, and National Pokédex No. 208.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon credit this Steelix to Benimaru Itoh.
Bulbapedia records Metal Crash for 50 damage with a coin-flip drawback and Rumble for 20 damage with a retreat-lock effect.

The promo's identity sits beside, but should not collapse into, the Japanese Gold/Silver to a New World Steelix row; the Trainer Magazine card has its own artist credit, source route, and border text.

The art matters because Benimaru Itoh's Steelix makes the new Metal typing feel physical and heavy, not merely a type icon; this is a different collector texture than the cleaner main-expansion Sugimori Steelix.
The card should be checked as the Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 5 bonus Steelix with Gold/Silver symbol, Benimaru Itoh credit, and Trainers Vol. 5 border text, not merely as a Japanese Steelix.

narrative.why_it_matters: Steelix is easy to flatten into a famous species name, but this promo deserves its own shape. It came through Pokemon Card Trainers Vol. 5, not a booster pack, and Benimaru Itoh makes the new Metal era feel massive: HP 100, Stage 1 from Onix, Metal Crash, Rumble, and a body compressed harder than diamond. It is a perfect agent test case because resemblance is dangerous here. The right card is not any Steelix. It is this magazine Steelix, with its route, artist, symbol, and bonus-card text still attached.
